nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set and $c : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a capacity function. The capacity of a subset $S \subseteq V$ is the total capacity of the arcs leaving $S$, $\sum_{u \in S} \sum_{v \in V \setminus S} c(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Cut capacity

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set, $s, t \in V$, and $f : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a function conserved at every vertex $v \ne s, t$, that is, $\sum_{u \in V} f(u, v) = \sum_{w \in V} f(v, w)$; no sign or capacity condition is imposed. nodes.title: Flow across a cut

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set, $c : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a capacity function and $s, t \in V$. If $f$ is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow for $c$ and $S$ is an $s$-$t$ cut, then the flow value of $f$ is at most the capacity of $S$ for $c$.
nodes.title: Weak duality for flows and cuts

nodes.summary: For a finite set $V$, a vertex $s \in V$ and a function $f : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$, the value of $f$ is its net outflow from the source $s$, $\sum_{v \in V} f(s, v) - \sum_{u \in V} f(u, s)$.
nodes.title: Flow value

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set, $c : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a capacity function and $s, t \in V$. A function $f : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow for $c$ if $0 \le f(u, v) \le c(u, v)$ for all $u, v \in V$ and $f$ is conserved at every vertex $v \ne s, t$, that is, $\sum_{u \in V} f(u, v) = \sum_{w \in V} f(v, w)$.
nodes.title: Feasible flow

nodes.summary: For a finite set $V$ and vertices $s, t \in V$, an $s$-$t$ cut is a subset $S \subseteq V$ with $s \in S$ and $t \notin S$.
nodes.title: Source–sink cut

nodes.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set, $c : V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ a capacity function with $c(u, v) \ge 0$ for all $u, v \in V$, and $s, t \in V$ with $s \ne t$. Then there is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow $f$ for $c$ whose value is at least the value of every feasible $s$-$t$ flow for $c$ and at most the capacity of every $s$-$t$ cut, and there is an $s$-$t$ cut whose capacity equals the value of $f$. nodes.title: Max-flow min-cut theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
